summary: The response directs Kernler to the response given to Witness 11 regarding why the Airport Spur wasn't built with I-94, and clarifies that the 125 land parcels and demolished homes were acquired for Mitchell Field's 60-acre air cargo area and have no connection to the Airport Spur proposal; it also details the FHWA-approved relocation program timeline and status.
text:
Please see the response to Witness 11 on page 236.

Questioned the acquisition of 125 land parcels and the demolishing of homes long before this public hearing.
The land and homes were acquired for Mitchell Field's 60 acre air cargo area and have no connection or relation to the Airport Spur proposal.
FHMA approval of the Division of Highways Relocation Program Plan was September 1969 and reaffirmed on August 1971 and March 1972. This plan consisted of 51 parcels, which required the relocation of 12 families and 4 businesses. 18 parcels, which included the relocation of 3 families and 2 businesses, have already been purchased. In March, 1973 right of way acquisition was suspended until the Final EIS was completed and approved. 33 parcels which include the relocation of 9 families and 2 businesses, remain to be relocated.

closing_anchor: 33 parcels which include the relocation of 9 families and 2 businesses, remain to be relocated.
